_note: Reference text for the plan, written from general knowledge and NOT verified live. Entry rules change often: check the official sources named below before travelling. Cite them in the thesis, not this file.

Visa and entry: Many European citizens travel under the Visa Waiver Program and need an approved ESTA before boarding (apply on the official site esta.cbp.dhs.gov; apply several days ahead). Other nationalities need a visa. Check travel.state.gov for your passport.
Passport should be valid for the whole stay; carry the return ticket and address of the first night.
SIM and internet: US prepaid SIMs and travel eSIMs are sold online and in stores (T-Mobile, AT&T, Verizon resellers). An eSIM bought before the flight works on arrival.
Free Wi-Fi is common in cafes and at universities, but do not rely on it for maps.
Payments: Cards and contactless payment are accepted nearly everywhere. Tipping (15 to 20 percent in restaurants) is expected and not included in the price.
Local transport: Public transport is slow between the sites: Caltrain connects San Francisco, Mountain View, Palo Alto and San Jose; BART serves Berkeley and Oakland. A Clipper card works on both.
Most company campuses are far from stations. Plan a rental car or ride-hail for the last leg, and allow for rush-hour traffic on US-101 and I-280.
